He played [[college football]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke Blue Devils]]. Jurgensen was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 1983. '''Leslie Herbert''' "'''Speedy'''" '''Duncan''' (August 10, 1942 – December 9, 2021) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] and [[return specialist]] in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Jackson State Tigers]]. Duncan played seven seasons with the [[San Diego Chargers]], where he was a three-time [[American Football League All-Star game|AFL All-Star]]. He was also named to the [[Pro Bowl]] with the [[Washington Commanders|Washington Redskins]]. Duncan was inducted into the [[Los Angeles Chargers Hall of Fame|Chargers Hall of Fame]] and was named to [[San Diego Chargers 40th Anniversary Team|their 40th]] and [[San Diego Chargers 50th Anniversary Team|50th anniversary teams]]. 

He was the first [[Punt (gridiron football)|punt]] returner in AFL history to return two punts for touchdowns in a season. His punt returning was so feared in the AFL, that it altered the way in which teams punted. He led the AFL in punt return average twice and the NFL once. He was the first player in AFL history to return an [[interception]] 100 yards for a touchdown.

'''Louis "Speedy" Timothy Thomas''' (April 13, 1947{{spaced ndash}}July 29, 2003<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/blogs/content/shared-gen/blogs/dayton/chickludwig/entries/2008/09/23/the_list_of_28_dead_bengals_pl.html |title=The List of 28 deceased Bengals players |author=Chick Ludwig |date=September 23, 2008 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |publisher= |access-date=October 23, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091001053848/http://www.daytondailynews.com/blogs/content/shared-gen/blogs/dayton/chickludwig/entries/2008/09/23/the_list_of_28_dead_bengals_pl.html |archive-date=October 1, 2009 }}
</ref>) was a professional [[American football]] [[wide receiver]] in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played for the AFL's [[Cincinnati Bengals]] (1969) and the NFL's Bengals (1970–1972) and [[New Orleans Saints]] (1973–1974).

Thomas played football at [[Booker T. Washington High School (Houston)|Booker T. Washington High School]] in [[Houston|Houston, Texas]].

He played [[college]] football at the [[University of Utah]]. During his senior season (1968), he was named first-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference]] (WAC), and he was selected to play in the annual all-star East-West Shrine Game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://graphics.fansonly.com/schools/utah/sports/m-footbl/archive/honors.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-01-26 |archive-date=2004-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040730050215/http://graphics.fansonly.com/schools/utah/sports/m-footbl/archive/honors.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was drafted in the third round (57th overall) of the [[1969 NFL/AFL draft]] by the second-year Cincinnati Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomSp00.htm|title = Speedy Thomas Stats| website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref>

In 1969, Thomas had a big rookie year as a flanker for the AFL's Bengals. Playing all 14 games, he had 33 receptions for 481 yards (a 14.6 average) and three touchdowns. He set a new Bengals record for receptions in a game with seven (for 177 yards) against the [[Denver Broncos]]. For the season, he also had four carries for 16 yards and a touchdown, and he returned four punts for 15 yards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1870&dat=19730709&id=OIQgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=ecwEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3472,3218638|title = Daytona Beach Sunday News-Journal - Google News Archive Search}}</ref>

His first professional touchdown was in week 2, when he caught a nine-yard touchdown pass from [[Greg Cook]] in a 24–30 win over the [[San Diego Chargers]].

In 1970, with the Bengals now in the NFL due to the NFL/AFL merger, he again played 14 games, including 13 as a starter at wide receiver. He had 21 receptions for 257 yards (a 12.2 average) and two touchdowns, along with two carries for seven yards and four punt returns for 20 yards.

In 1971, he played 12 games, starting eight as wide receiver. He had 22 receptions for 327 yards (a 14.9 average). He also had his longest career reception and the longest in the NFL in 1971—a 90-yard touchdown pass from [[Virgil Carter]] in the season-opening game, a 37–14 win over the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He also returned four punts for 20 yards and had two carries for -1 yards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomSp00.htm|title = Speedy Thomas Stats| website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref>

In 1972, he played in 11 games, starting 10. He had 17 receptions for 171 yards (a 10.1 average) and one touchdown.

After four years with the Bengals, on July 9, 1973, he was traded to the New Orleans Saints for rookie [[defensive tackle]] [[Jerry Ellison]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1454&dat=19730710&id=A2s0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=siYEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4432,2546694|title = Star-News - Google News Archive Search}}</ref>

In 1973 for the Saints, he played in six games with no statistics. In 1974, his sixth and last in pro football, he played in one game, with one reception for three yards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomSp00.htm|title = Speedy Thomas Stats| website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref>

'''Denman Preston Gordon''' (July 30, 1965 – April 26, 2023) was an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

Gordon was born in [[Lynn, Massachusetts]],<ref name="PFR1">{{Cite web |title=Sonny Gordon Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GordSo20.htm |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> but attended [[Middletown High School (Ohio)|Middletown High School]] in [[Middletown, Ohio|Ohio]]. He was both a basketball and football standout, as well as president of his senior class.<ref name="HJN">{{cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.com/former-middletown-high-standout-athlete-141400285.html |title=Former Middletown High standout athlete, class president dies from ALS |publisher=Hamilton (OH) Journal-News |date=April 29, 2023 |access-date=May 25, 2024 |via=Yahoo Sports}}</ref>

He played [[college football|collegiately]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]],<ref name="NFL">{{cite web| url=https://www.nfl.com/players/sonny-gordon/ |title=Sonny Gordon Stats |website=NFL.com |access-date=May 25, 2024}}</ref> where, as a senior, he was honored by [[Gannett News Service]] as a third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref name="GNS 1986">{{cite news |title=Gannette (sic) News Service All-Americans |newspaper=Iowa City Press-Citizen |date=December 2, 1986 |page=2b |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/iowa-city-press-citizen-1986-gannett-all/147669728/ |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Gordon was selected by his hometown [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the sixth round of the [[1987 NFL draft]],<ref name="PFR2">{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> but was released at the final roster cuts. He signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and appeared in seven games for them.<ref name="PFR1"/>

Gordon was out of professional football during the 1988 season, but joined the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the CFL the following year. He appeared in 33 games for the Tiger-Cats, over the course of two seasons, recording four interceptions, three of which he returned for touchdowns. He finished his career playing a single season with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] in 1991.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerg/gord01600.html |title=Sonny Gordon Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=May 25, 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231113035602/https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerg/gord01600.html |archive-date=November 13, 2023}}</ref>

Gordon died from [[amyotrophic lateral sclerosis]], in [[Dublin, Ohio]], on April 26, 2023. He was 57.<ref name="HJN"/><ref name="PFA"/>
